title: Mystery Bulk Book Orders Raise Questions About AI Data Needs
subtitle: Secondhand booksellers around the world are seeing strange, large orders that they believe are linked to artificial intelligence companies.

summary.en: Secondhand booksellers in the UK, Ireland, and other countries are reporting a sudden increase in large, unusual book orders. These buyers often request random titles that do not follow normal shopping patterns. Many shop owners believe these orders are being placed by artificial intelligence companies. These companies may be buying the books to scan their text for training AI models. This trend is changing how the secondhand book market operates.
summary.zh: 英國、愛爾蘭及其他國家的二手書商回報，大量且不尋常的書籍訂單突然增加。這些買家通常要求隨機的書目，不符合一般的購物模式。許多店主認為這些訂單是由人工智慧公司所下達。這些公司可能是為了掃描書中文字以訓練人工智慧模型。此趨勢正在改變二手書市場的運作方式。

paragraphs.en: Secondhand booksellers across the globe are facing a strange new trend. Shops in the UK, Ireland, Australia, and the United States have reported a sudden wave of large, bulk orders from mysterious buyers. Unlike typical customers who might look for books on a specific topic like history or cooking, these buyers are requesting a random mix of titles. This has led many shop owners to suspect that artificial intelligence (AI) companies are behind the purchases.
paragraphs.zh: 全球各地的二手書店正面臨一種奇特的新趨勢。英國、愛爾蘭、澳洲與美國的店家紛紛回報，出現了一波來自神秘買家的突發性大量採購潮。與一般會尋找歷史或烹飪等特定主題書籍的顧客不同，這些買家要求的是隨機組合的書目。這讓許多店主懷疑，人工智慧公司正是這些採購行為背後的推手。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, these orders began to appear in significant numbers earlier this year. Stuart Manley, the co-owner of Barter Books in the UK, noted that the requests are very unusual. He explained that a single order might include an Estonian translation of a novel, a specific old edition of a classic book, and a magazine from the 1980s. Manley said that these items do not follow any logical theme, which is very different from how people usually buy books.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報 (The Guardian)》報導，這些訂單在今年稍早開始大量出現。英國「以物易物書店 (Barter Books)」的共同店主史都華·曼利 (Stuart Manley) 指出，這些需求非常不尋常。他解釋說，單筆訂單可能同時包含一本小說的愛沙尼亞語譯本、某本經典書籍的特定舊版，以及一本 1980 年代的雜誌。曼利表示，這些項目完全沒有邏輯主題可言，這與人們平時買書的方式大相逕庭。

paragraphs.en: Other booksellers have shared similar experiences. Jim Shaughnessy, who owns MW Books in Ireland, said his shop has been receiving large and varied orders since May. He described the orders as "sporadic" and likely driven by machines rather than humans. He noted that the requests cover a massive range of subjects, from farming tools in 18th-century Africa to the lives of 1950s race car drivers. While he does not feel it is his place to tell customers what to do with their money, he admitted that the situation is very curious.
paragraphs.zh: 其他書商也分享了類似的經歷。在愛爾蘭經營「MW 圖書 (MW Books)」的吉姆·蕭內西 (Jim Shaughnessy) 表示，他的店自五月以來就不斷收到龐大且雜亂的訂單。他形容這些訂單「零星且不連貫」，很可能是由機器而非人類所驅動。他注意到這些需求涵蓋了極廣的領域，從 18 世紀非洲的農具到 1950 年代賽車手的生平應有盡有。雖然他認為自己無權過問顧客如何花錢，但他坦言這種情況確實非常令人好奇。

paragraphs.en: There is growing speculation that these companies are buying the books to feed data into AI systems. Artificial intelligence models require vast amounts of text to learn how to communicate and process information. By purchasing physical books, these companies can scan the pages to turn them into digital data. Once the information is captured, the physical books are often destroyed or "pulped." Stuart Manley shared his own theory, suggesting that large amounts of money from the AI industry are being spent to acquire this information.
paragraphs.zh: 外界越來越多猜測認為，這些公司買書是為了將內容輸入人工智慧系統。人工智慧模型需要海量的文字來學習如何溝通與處理資訊。透過購買實體書，這些公司可以掃描書頁並將其轉化為數位資料。一旦資訊被擷取，實體書往往會被銷毀或「打成紙漿」。史都華·曼利分享了他的個人觀點，認為人工智慧產業正投入大筆資金來獲取這些資訊。

paragraphs.en: This trend is causing real problems for the secondhand book trade. David Gower-Spence, the owner of BookLovers of Bath, said he received a rush of orders for about 200 books between May and July. He described the experience as "overwhelming." Another bookseller, who asked to remain anonymous, reported receiving orders for 6,000 books since January. This seller noted that the buyers are willing to pay high prices and do not ask for discounts, even when buying in bulk. This behavior is not typical for the trade and is disrupting normal business operations.
paragraphs.zh: 這種趨勢正對二手書交易造成實質困擾。巴斯市「愛書人 (BookLovers of Bath)」的店主大衛·高爾-史賓斯 (David Gower-Spence) 表示，他在五月到七月間收到了一波約 200 本書的急單，他形容這種體驗「令人難以招架」。另一位要求匿名的書商則回報，自一月以來已收到總計 6,000 本書的訂單。這位賣家指出，買家願意支付高價且不要求折扣，即使是大量採購也是如此。這種行為在該行業並不常見，且已干擾了正常的商業運作。

paragraphs.en: Some of the details about these buyers are also quite mysterious. The anonymous bookseller mentioned that the names used for these orders are very difficult to identify. Furthermore, different buyers have been seen using the same delivery address, which points to freight warehouses near Heathrow airport in the UK. One company, Canada-based Zoom Books, has been identified in reports as being involved in these orders. Zoom Books describes itself as a "book recycling company," but it has not provided further details about its clients.
paragraphs.zh: 關於這些買家的部分細節也相當神秘。該名匿名書商提到，這些訂單所使用的名稱非常難以辨識。此外，不同買家被發現使用相同的寄送地址，指向英國希斯洛機場 (Heathrow Airport) 附近的貨運倉庫。其中一家名為「Zoom Books」的加拿大公司，在報導中被指名與這些訂單有關。Zoom Books 將自己描述為一家「圖書回收公司」，但並未提供關於其客戶的進一步細節。

paragraphs.en: As the demand continues, booksellers are struggling to keep up. One Australian bookseller told The Guardian that the sudden scale of these requests is "driving me nuts." Because the orders are so random and large, they do not fit into the usual market trends. This makes it hard for shop owners to manage their inventory and plan for their regular customers.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著需求持續增加，書商們正疲於應付。一位澳洲書商告訴《衛報》，這些需求突如其來的規模讓他「快要瘋了」。由於訂單如此隨機且龐大，它們完全不符合一般的市場趨勢。這使得店主難以管理庫存，也難以為常客規劃服務。

paragraphs.en: What will happen next remains unclear. For now, the secondhand book market is dealing with a situation that feels more like a mystery than a normal business transaction. Whether these AI companies will continue to buy books in such large amounts depends on their ongoing need for new data. For the booksellers, the priority is simply managing the high volume of requests while trying to understand who is really behind these strange, machine-like orders. As the industry watches, the link between old books and new technology continues to grow, changing the way we think about the value of printed paper in the digital age.
paragraphs.zh: 接下來會發生什麼事仍不明朗。目前，二手書市場正處理著一種比起商業交易更像謎團的情況。這些人工智慧公司是否會繼續大量購買書籍，取決於它們對新資料的持續需求。對書商而言，當務之急只是應付龐大的訂單量，同時試圖釐清到底是誰在這些奇怪、機械式的訂單背後操盤。隨著業界持續關注，舊書與新科技之間的連結不斷加深，也正在改變我們在數位時代對紙本印刷品價值的看法。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To reduce paper or books to a soft, wet mass in order to recycle it.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 將紙張或書籍打成紙漿（以便回收）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 此詞在日常生活中較少見，這裡指書籍被銷毀並回收。文中：Once the information is captured, the physical books are often destroyed or "pulped."

keyTerms.definitionEn: Making someone feel very annoyed, frustrated, or crazy.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 讓我快瘋了、讓我非常煩躁。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是口語化的慣用語，字面上與「駕駛」或「堅果」無關。文中：One Australian bookseller told The Guardian that the sudden scale of these requests is "driving me nuts."

keyTerms.definitionEn: Responsible for or the cause of something.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 是……的幕後主使、造成……的原因。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作方位介詞（在……後面），這裡指「幕後黑手」或「背後推手」。文中：This has led many shop owners to suspect that artificial intelligence (AI) companies are behind the purchases.

quiz.question: According to the article, what common characteristic do the mysterious bulk orders share?

options.A: They consist exclusively of rare 18th-century historical documents.
options.B: They contain a random assortment of titles without a logical theme.
options.C: They are placed only by individuals living near Heathrow airport.
options.D: They are always requested by customers seeking to resell them at a profit.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，Stuart Manley 指出這些訂單包含極為隨機的項目（如愛沙尼亞語小說、舊雜誌等），且沒有任何邏輯主題，這與一般顧客的購買行為大相徑庭。選項 A 錯誤，因為訂單範圍極廣，不限於歷史文件；選項 C 錯誤，文中僅提到送貨地址指向這些區域，並未說買家皆居住於此；選項 D 文中並未提及買家的轉售動機，僅提到他們願意支付高價。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the impact of these bulk orders on secondhand bookstore owners?

options.A: They are happy because the high prices help them clear out unwanted inventory.
options.B: They are worried that their shops will be forced to close due to legal action.
options.C: They find it difficult to manage their regular business operations and inventory.
options.D: They are actively collaborating with AI companies to digitize their collections.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第七段，書商提到這些隨機且大量的訂單讓他們難以管理庫存並規劃一般顧客的需求，甚至有人表示這讓他們感到「快瘋了」（driving me nuts）。選項 A 錯誤，雖然買家願意付高價，但書商感到的是負擔而非開心；選項 B 錯誤，文中未提及法律問題；選項 D 錯誤，書商與買家並非合作關係，書商對這些訂單感到困惑且不知情。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'pulped' mean in the context of the physical books?

options.A: To be recycled or destroyed after the information is scanned.
options.B: To be carefully preserved in a digital library for future use.
options.C: To be sold to other bookstores at a significant discount.
options.D: To be cleaned and repaired to look like new editions.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在第四段中，提到 AI 公司購買書籍是為了掃描其中的資料，一旦資訊被擷取，這些實體書通常會被銷毀或「打成紙漿」（pulped）。這是一個非字面意義的用法，指將書籍作為廢紙處理。選項 B 與原文意思相反；選項 C 錯誤，文中並未提及轉賣；選項 D 錯誤，這與文章提到書籍被處理掉的脈絡不符。

quiz.question: What is the central message of this article?

options.A: Secondhand bookstores are becoming the primary source of income for AI developers.
options.B: The rise of AI is creating a mysterious and disruptive trend in the secondhand book trade.
options.C: Bookstores in the UK and Ireland are struggling because people no longer read physical books.
options.D: AI companies are intentionally trying to destroy the global secondhand book market.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。本文主要探討全球二手書店面臨的一種新趨勢，即神秘買家（疑似為 AI 公司）大量收購隨機書籍以獲取數據，這對傳統二手書商的經營模式造成了困擾與混亂。選項 A 誇大了影響；選項 C 錯誤，問題在於「大量購買」而非「沒人買書」；選項 D 錯誤，文中並未指出 AI 公司有「意圖」摧毀市場，這只是其行為帶來的負面副作用。
